story: In 1984, at the American embassy in Moscow and the consulate in Leningrad, sixteen IBM Selectric typewriters were found that had spent eight years retelling everything typed on them. A bug in a metal bar caught the movements of the mechanism: four bits per keystroke, several letters to each sound. What exactly had been typed, the post rebuilt by the laws of probability. How I came upon this story is {blog}.
bug: The real scheme was never published. My bug has sixteen sounds, two or three letters to each, and the post knows only the {count} words Vova’s sites are written in (the dictionary was built at commit {commit}). A word it doesn’t know, it won’t guess.
typeHint: Type anything, in English or Russian
sample: Hi everyone, I’m Maya from za/oblozhkoy. We don’t exist, but we hope that won’t stop you from enjoying our music.
unknown: The post doesn’t know this word
tally: {right} of {total} right. Red is a wrong guess, underlined could read otherwise, grey is a word the post doesn’t know.
